conventions: The closing formula 'Now the rest of the acts of X … are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel/Judah' (14.15, 14.18, 14.28) divides: waw → Now; יֶתֶר → the rest; דִּבְרֵי → of the acts (middle construct with of and supplied the); הֲ → are (fronted copula, rule 20); הֵם → they; כְּתוּבִים → written; עַל → in; סֵפֶר → the book; דִּבְרֵי + הַיָּמִים → of chronicles fused on the construct with the article taking its own the; לְ → of; מַלְכֵי → the kings. Additional clauses inside the frame ('and how he fought/warred') give how to each אֲשֶׁר and the pronoun to the verb.

Appositional even: 'even thou' (14.10) is added because the pronoun stands bare with no marker, waw or preposition; 'even with the kings of Israel' (14.29) keeps even with the second עִם as that preposition's expanded rendering under rule 16, headed on with. Read whether a preposition stands under the even before choosing.

תַּחְתָּיו in the succession formula is 'in … stead' on the preposition, discontinuous around the suffix's his (14.16, 14.29); the fuller 'in the room of' (14.21) is the same preposition headed on room under rule 24.
report: Read all 57 candidate groups and the six added units end to end. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently (waw → And/but/So/Now/for/that/also; article the/that which/who/unrepresented by whether a the or a relative is written; be → in/at/by/for/from; אֵת → of only in 14.7 where the ASV spends a word on the object relation). No construction is analysed two ways in this chapter.

Recurring formulae are internally consistent: the 'rest of the acts … chronicles of the kings' frame (15, 18, 28) divides identically each time; compound numerals 15/16 fuse as one word in 17, 21, 23; 'in his stead' (16, 29) and 'made king' (21) are uniform; the age formula gives the copula to a written haya (14.2) and to ben where no verb stands (14.21), as rule 58 directs.

Added units are consistent with each other: the 'even' of 14.10 stands before a bare pronoun with no morpheme to carry it and is added, while the 'even with' of 14.29 stands on a second עִם and is kept with the preposition under rule 16's expanded-preposition reading; 'which' in 14.28 is added where no relative is written, while 'which' in 14.11 goes to the written אֲשֶׁר.

BSB disagreements (18) are all documented convention: object markers, le of le'mor, a be whose object the ASV promotes (14.13), articles the ASV writes no the for, paragogic he, the suffix silenced by 'home' (14.10), the waw of a pronoun recast as relative (14.21), and the trailing absolute shanah of a regnal date (14.23). None is a genuine error.

One single-verse reading worth a later look, not a split and not patched here: 14.22 gives the 'that' of 'after that the king slept' to the infinitive, citing rule 19, but אַחֲרֵי is tagged R with no construct noun between it and the infinitive, so rule 52's first paragraph would put the complementizer on the preposition as 'after that'. Either placement leaves every id partitioned; the verse note records its reasoning.
